standard.title: Cohesion through paragraph structure
standard.description: understand how cohesion in texts is improved by strengthening the internal structure of paragraphs with examples, quotations and substantiation of claims
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify how cohesive devices (e.g. connectives, reference chains) create flow within and between paragraphs (AC9E7LA04). They have not yet examined how the internal structure of paragraphs — claim, example, quotation, substantiation — creates the logical coherence that cohesion depends on.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand how strengthening paragraph internal structure through examples, quotations and substantiation improves textual cohesion.

nodes.label: Paragraph internal structure
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the structural components of a well-formed paragraph (claim/topic sentence, example, evidence/quotation, substantiation/explanation) and explain how each component contributes to the paragraph's coherence.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the claim, example and substantiation in one provided paragraph and explain how they work together to develop a point.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain how claims, examples, quotations and substantiation function together in extended analytical paragraphs, including understanding how the substantiation step connects evidence back to the claim.
wider: Compare a well-substantiated paragraph with one that makes a claim but lacks explanation, and analyse what is lost without the substantiation step
Examine how academic writing in different disciplines (e.g. science report vs literary analysis) uses different conventions for substantiating claims
Annotate a peer's or published paragraph, identifying each structural component and evaluating the effectiveness of the substantiation

response_modes.reason: Students commonly write claim + quote with no explanation, treating quotation as self-evidently supporting the claim. Explicit scaffolding of the claim-example-substantiation chain — and why each step matters — is needed before students can execute it reliably.

success_criteria: Identifies the claim, at least one piece of evidence (example or quotation) and the substantiation step in a given paragraph.
Explains how the substantiation connects the evidence back to the paragraph's claim.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to write substantiated paragraphs and explain how they improve textual cohesion — a consolidation task that depends entirely on understanding the claim-example-substantiation chain at Node 1. Students who have not grasped the structure have nothing to consolidate.

nodes.label: Substantiation improving cohesion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how strengthened paragraph internal structure — particularly the inclusion of substantiation — improves overall textual cohesion by ensuring each paragraph fully develops its contribution to the text.
nodes.minimum_width: Revise or extend one underdeveloped paragraph by adding substantiation, and explain how the revision improves the paragraph's contribution to the text as a whole.
nodes.typical_width: Write or revise extended analytical paragraphs that use claim, example, quotation and substantiation effectively, explaining how well-developed paragraph structure contributes to the cohesion of a longer analytical text.
wider: Investigate how argument cohesion depends on each paragraph fully substantiating its claim — how a single under-substantiated paragraph disrupts the logical chain of an entire text
Write a multi-paragraph analytical text and review its cohesion by tracing whether each claim is fully substantiated and whether the paragraph sequence creates a coherent progression of ideas
Examine how formal debate speeches or published opinion writing use substantiation differently from academic essays

response_modes.reason: Paragraph substantiation is a fluency skill — knowing the structure intellectually is not enough. Students need repeated practice writing and revising paragraphs before the pattern becomes automatic. Consolidation at this node (writing multiple paragraphs, revising for substantiation) builds the fluency that transfers to independent writing.

success_criteria: Produces an extended analytical paragraph that includes a clear claim, at least one piece of evidence and an explicit substantiation connecting evidence to claim.
Can explain how their paragraph contributes to the cohesion of a longer text.
